program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s criterion and traces support “complete”: the edited image visibly places a frog inside the toilet bowl, while the source has none. The reference “partial” conflicts with that evidence, but is only an aggregate constraint, not atomic ground truth; do not force a partial verdict or weaken the placement requirement to match it. Investigate whether the evaluator’s partial label reflects an unstated criterion or a reference/evaluation mismatch, and ensure the node distinguishes a frog inside the bowl from frogs merely on the lid or floor. The repeated high-confidence traces show stable visual judgment, not missing progress; there are no transport, schema, or dependency failures indicated. Clarify the binding/question only if needed to make the requested placement and complete-versus-partial boundary explicit, while preserving uncertainty for genuinely ambiguous placement.
